title: Cotton Club break when Duke went to California; the Savoy deal
summary: The band took Duke's place, and the Savoy and Moe Gale's concessions paid fifty dollars a week.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah, right. So see, we got in the Cotton Club when Duke Ellington made the trip to California to make a movie.
I thought it was Three Little Words. I always thought...

I think it was Three Little Words. We can check it. Anyway, Mills got involved with the band through Moe Gale, who was at the Savoy. See, we kind of like... We belonged to the Savoy. I didn't know the business side of it, but the Savoy took the band over. And we used to make fifty dollars a week when we played one day, one night, two nights or three nights. They got some concessions going at the Alhambra Ballroom, and they used to book affairs up there. So we were the band that would play up there. Then sometimes we'd play on Sunday at the Savoy. So most of the nights they booked was like Friday and Saturday at the Alhambra. And we didn't play but one date or two dates. We made fifty dollars a week. And you know, we were getting more money than some of them bands that was playing all week at the Savoy. See, the Savoy worked out a deal where they didn't have to pay the bands that worked there all week... I think it was thirty-three dollars and...
And we were making fifty dollars. So we were kind of living high on the hog, you know.
